Adding a digital version of your driver's license to iPhone looks set to expand to a 15th US state in the near future.

Apple currently lists 14 states that support the feature, along with the territory of Puerto Rico, but backend data suggests one more is on the way...

Many of us have long hoped for a future where we no longer need to carry physical forms of identification like driver's licenses and passports, and can simply present digital ID directly from our iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be quite far off, but Apple took the first step back in 2021, when the company announced plans to let iPhone users add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. 14 states have since adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors suggests that Oklahoma will be joining the list soon.

We previously detailed the steps for adding your driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As we noted at the time, it's worth being aware that digital IDs may not fully replace the physical version, so unfortunately we'd still recommend you continue to carry it.

That said, the digital version can still help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints and when proving your age to a vendor. The ID will simply confirm you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal details like your date of birth.
